task_payload.focus: Audit Click's public export layer, decorators, command core, parser, and testing harness.

task_results.notes: Proven facts: click.__init__ is the public export layer, command/group decorators turn callables into Command/Group objects, Command.main -> make_context -> parse_args -> invoke is the top-level control path, Group.invoke resolves subcommands through get_command/resolve_command, and CliRunner isolation mutates global stdio/env state and is explicitly single-threaded. Proven risks: CliRunner global-state mutation and the docs warning that lazy loading can trigger circular-import bugs. Hypothesis: callable-type inference is a brittle seam because unknown callables always route through convert_type/FuncParamType.
evidence: src/click/__init__.py:10-75 re-exports core, decorators, termui, types, and utils; __getattr__ handles deprecated names at 77-124.
src/click/decorators.py:217-249 builds Command objects from decorated callables after collecting __click_params__.
src/click/core.py:1210-1298 and 1366-1445 show make_context -> parse_args -> invoke inside Command.main.
src/click/core.py:1806-1959 shows Group.get_command, Group.invoke, and resolve_command for subcommand dispatch.
src/click/testing.py:261-345 and 525-636 show IO/environment isolation and CliRunner.invoke plumbing.

task_payload.flow: Explain what happens when setup_panic!() is installed and a release-mode panic occurs.

task_results.notes: setup_panic!() expands to setup_panic(|| metadata), setup_panic() installs a panic hook only in PanicStyle::Human, the hook builds Report::with_panic, persists report-NNN.toml under env::temp_dir() when not in CI, and then prints the human message to stderr. In CI, persistence is skipped and the serialized TOML report is emitted to stderr before the user-facing message.

task_payload.symptom: A callable instance used as a custom Click option type crashes during command construction with AttributeError because the object has no __name__ attribute.

task_payload.bug: The lane workspace contains a seeded regression test proving callable instances should work as custom option types.

task_payload.refactor_scope: Queue scheduling and draining helpers only.

task_results.notes: Hidden coupling is concentrated inside index.js: resumeNext increments activeCount and dequeues work, next decrements and pumps again, enqueue bridges queue items to Promise resolution, clearQueue drains pending work, and the concurrency setter also pumps resumeNext in a microtask. Safe ordering: extract a drainPending helper first, then a scheduler pump helper, while leaving next() semantics in place until tests pass. Rollback/proof boundary is a single runtime file plus clearQueue/concurrency tests and the tsd signature file.

index.js:50-63 defines enqueue, which decides when pending work becomes runnable.
index.js:77-89 clearQueue and 91-104 concurrency setter both manipulate queue draining behavior.
test.js:184-214 and 305-340 already cover clearQueue and concurrency changes and would be the first proof boundary after any refactor.

task_payload.claim: README/docs say Click supports lazy loading of subcommands at runtime.

task_results.notes: No hard documentation drift: the top-level README/index claim is shorthand, while docs/complex accurately explains that lazy loading is achieved by a custom Group subclass overriding list_commands/get_command. Code truth is that the default Group implementation only returns already-registered commands from self.commands, so lazy loading is supported as an extension pattern rather than as default built-in behavior.
evidence: README.md:16-18 and docs/index.rst:19-23 make the top-level “supports lazy loading” claim.
docs/complex.md:224-355 shows the actual supported pattern: a custom LazyGroup overriding list_commands/get_command and doing imports there.
src/click/core.py:1806-1810 returns self.commands.get(cmd_name), and resolve_command at 1935-1959 just asks get_command to resolve the subcommand.
